text:
maya: quick heads-up — we're onboarding Idyl-13B into the eval queue. spotted a license addendum that looks non-standard, want a fast legal check before we run large quant + perf jobs.

samir: what does the addendum say? redistrib banned?

maya: the header is CC-BY-NC-4.0 but there's an extra clause: 'embeddings may be allowed for commercial use if attribution is displayed; redistribution of model weights or quantized binaries is prohibited without an express commercial license.' link: https://example.idyl/license.txt

liz: reading it now. cc-by-nc with an extra sentence = potentially ambiguous. need the exact clause text, but high-level: NC restricts commercial use of the model itself, but they carved out embeddings — that matters.

noah: if embeddings are allowed commercially, product-wise we can serve embedding API on Hosted/Dedicated. question: can we ship quantized weights to Dedicated customers or include them in Private deploy packages?

samir: technically, for Dedicated we sometimes hand over docker images with model artifacts for on-prem node pools. Private customers get full model bundles if the contract permits. this clause might block us from packaging qweights into a customer-delivered binary.

liz: correct: 'redistribution of model weights or quantized binaries is prohibited' reads as a blanket ban. But the embedding carve-out means running the model to produce embeddings for customers may be allowed. Important distinctions: (A) hosting/serving the model (i.e., providing API results) vs (B) handing over the weights/binaries. The license forbids (B) unless we negotiate.

maya: re: quantization experiments — if we quantize Idyl for internal perf testing and publish benchmarks (no weight sharing), is that allowed? we typically run evals on internal infra and publish numbers + eval artifacts.

liz: publishing benchmark numbers is fine. just do not publish quantized weights or docker images that contain them. Also avoid publishing scripts that trivially reconstruct or point to internal artifacts. Attribute the model per CC-BY terms.

noah: what about caching layers and third-party CDNs? e.g., we cache token prefixes / kv caches in a shared cache that might persist derived artifacts. could that be interpreted as redistribution?

samir: our caches never store full weights, but we do persist intermediate KV shards and prompt prefixes. not the model artifact itself.

liz: legally those caches are not 'model weights' so they're fine. the risk is if we export a cached snapshot that could be rehydrated to approximate the model. unlikely, but avoid shipping any cache snapshots externally.

maya: ok good. another ask: some of our Dedicated customers request an offline bundle (tar.gz) for air-gapped installs. license seems to prohibit that unless we sign a commercial addendum. default behaviour for Idyl should be: Hosted and Dedicated serving OK, but do NOT include model files in customer-delivered bundles without legal sign-off.

liz: agreed. if a customer needs offline/binary delivery, escalate to legal sales & create a paid license addendum. we can draft a standard commercial redistribution addendum that permits qweights shipping under terms (e.g., no sublicensing, attribution, audit rights).

noah: attribution UI — Legal wants a specific string? We should make it easy for engineers to add.

liz: CC-BY requires attribution. the additional clause requires a visible attribution when customers consume embeddings commercially. Suggested minimal text (ok to include in API docs or UI):

```
Model: Idyl-13B by IdylAI. Licensed under CC-BY-NC-4.0 with additional commercial embedding permission. See https://example.idyl/license.txt for details.
```

liz: include a link to the license and a short notice in the API response headers for embedding responses: `X-Model-Attribution: "Idyl-13B (IdylAI); license: https://example.idyl/license.txt"`

samir: small tech note: adding headers is easy for Hosted. For Dedicated we need a config flag in the serving runtime to inject attribution into embedding responses. will add a flag to the model manifest.

maya: for evals we also sometimes share validation prompts and metric plots on public repo. liz, is it ok to publish prompt sets + eval code?

liz: yes publish prompts and eval results. just scrub any internal dataset rows that are private. do not include model artifacts or links to internal model download endpoints. Also include the attribution snippet in the repo README and in published benchmark notes.

deploy-bot: snapshot created for thread 3791234567: ci/bench/idyl13b/q-run-20260321 (artifacts: logs, metrics) :white_check_mark:

maya: next steps: (1) @liz can you propose a short addendum template for redistribution of quantized weights (so sales can reuse)? (2) @samir, add attribute injection flag to serving manifest and block any packaging step that bundles model binaries without an explicit label. (3) I'll rerun quant evals with no artifact exports and publish numbers + attribution text.

liz: will draft addendum today and drop it in #legal-templates, tagging sales. rough bullets: permitted redistribution under signed addendum, restrictions on sublicensing, mandatory attribution, audit rights, and fees.

samir: will add a pre-flight check in our build pipeline to fail packaging if model.json `license.prohibits_redistribution == true`. quick PR incoming.

maya: awesome — thanks everyone. filing a follow-up doc for onboarding checklist with the license constraints so we don't accidentally ship qweights.

noah: thanks — can we also capture a short FAQ for non-technical teams (sales/customer success) about what 'embeddings allowed' means vs 'weights not allowed'? I can draft after liz's addendum.

liz: yes, I'll give a 2-line explainer they can paste into SOWs.

maya: ping me when the checklist & addendum are up, then we lift the hold on perf runs. :thumbsup:
